_doc: Purpose-specific rewrite of the original 23 judge-panel cases. Original titles, keep/reject labels, confidence and mechanisms are preserved. Historical claims are benchmark data, not verified current product knowledge. The former idempotency post-mortem lacks an incident account and is a troubleshooting pattern. Metrics are not comparable to the shorthand corpus until this version is rebaselined.

cases.label: keep
cases.title: pgtype.Text{} is NULL not empty string, breaks $1='' filters
cases.summary: pgtype.Text{} is NULL not empty string, breaks $1='' filters

sections.symptoms: An unset pgtype.Text value does not match a filter that tests $1=''.
sections.diagnosis: Distinguish a NULL parameter from the empty string when interpreting the filter.
sections.cause: The original case states that pgtype.Text{} marshals to NULL, so the equality predicate never matches it.
sections.remedy: Use IS NULL or an explicit sentinel for the intended unset-value behavior.
sections.verification: The historical case gives the mechanism but no current test run or driver revision; those remain unverified.

cases.label: keep
cases.title: Mollie webhooks are unsigned, re-fetch the payment by id
cases.summary: Mollie webhooks are unsigned, re-fetch the payment by id

sections.context: The callback is used to decide whether a payment authorizes an account grant.
sections.options: The case contrasts trusting the webhook body or metadata with retrieving the payment by its ID. It states that no callback HMAC is available.
sections.decision: Retrieve GET /v2/payments/{id} before granting anything, and base the grant on that payment record.
sections.rationale: The original evidence states that an unsigned callback can be forged to self-upgrade an account.
sections.consequences: The grant depends on a payment lookup rather than untrusted callback claims. Provider behavior and the actual integration revision need rechecking before reuse.

cases.label: keep
cases.title: SSRF denylist must include 100.64.0.0/10 (Tailscale CGNAT)
cases.summary: SSRF denylist must include 100.64.0.0/10 (Tailscale CGNAT)

sections.symptoms: A submitted public URL can redirect to a tailnet host, causing the fetcher to return an internal response.
sections.diagnosis: Evaluate the resolved connection IP on every redirect hop, including the 100.64.0.0/10 CGNAT range.
sections.cause: The historical case identifies redirect-following and validation of only the initial URL as the bypass mechanism.
sections.remedy: Reject the CGNAT range on the actual resolved connection address for each hop.
sections.verification: No current redirect test, DNS setup or network topology is supplied by this fixture.

cases.label: keep
cases.title: Broken YAML frontmatter silently drops a note from the index
cases.summary: Broken YAML frontmatter silently drops a note from the index

sections.symptoms: A Markdown note exists on disk but is absent from search and the graph.
sections.diagnosis: Check frontmatter parsing, including unquoted values containing colon-space, and surface indexing parse errors.
sections.cause: The original case reports that ParseFiles skipped unparseable notes without warning. This is historical evidence, not a statement about the current implementation.
sections.remedy: Quote affected YAML values and report parse failures during indexing.
sections.verification: The original case includes no current parser revision or repaired-note retrieval result.

cases.label: keep
cases.title: Go base64-encodes []byte in JSON responses
cases.summary: Go base64-encodes []byte in JSON responses

sections.symptoms: A JSONB value returned through a []byte response field becomes a base64 string rather than raw JSON.
sections.diagnosis: Check the Go field type used by encoding/json at the serialization boundary.
sections.cause: The case states that encoding/json base64-encodes []byte values, changing JSONB round-trip behavior.
sections.remedy: Use json.RawMessage for JSON content or convert it deliberately before serialization.
sections.verification: No concrete payload round-trip or application revision accompanies the original fixture.

cases.label: keep
cases.title: SQLite WAL never truncates itself, journal_size_limit caps it
cases.summary: SQLite WAL never truncates itself, journal_size_limit caps it

sections.symptoms: A SQLite WAL file remains large after passive checkpointing.
sections.diagnosis: Distinguish resetting the write position from shrinking the file on disk.
sections.cause: The original case states that passive checkpointing resets the write pointer without shrinking the WAL file.
sections.remedy: Set journal_size_limit and use a TRUNCATE checkpoint at clean shutdown in the applicable setup.
sections.verification: The fixture supplies no workload, active-reader state or measured WAL sizes; the title's broad claim is retained as historical benchmark input.

cases.label: keep
cases.title: chi RealIP trusts X-Forwarded-For from any upstream
cases.summary: chi RealIP trusts X-Forwarded-For from any upstream

sections.symptoms: A client can spoof the source IP used for rate limiting through X-Forwarded-For.
sections.diagnosis: Check which upstream sources the chi RealIP configuration trusts before using its result as a rate-limit identity.
sections.cause: The case attributes the spoofing mechanism to accepting XFF from any upstream.
sections.remedy: Restrict proxy trust to the configured trusted proxy CIDR before rate limiting on the derived IP.
sections.verification: No current middleware revision, trusted-proxy configuration or spoofing test result is supplied.

cases.label: keep
cases.title: Extraction judge must be a different model than the extractor
cases.summary: Extraction judge must be a different model than the extractor

sections.context: An extraction benchmark needs to measure whether candidates are useful, rather than whether the extractor approves its own output.
sections.options: The original case contrasts self-grading with using an independent model configured through MESH_JUDGE_*.
sections.decision: Use an independent model when grading extraction precision.
sections.rationale: The original evidence reports that self-grading rubber-stamped the model's own candidates and yielded approximately 100 percent.
sections.consequences: The measured precision needs an independent assessment; this fixture provides no new baseline or model comparison.

cases.label: keep
cases.title: em dashes in a value break sqlc code generation
cases.summary: em dashes in a value break sqlc code generation

sections.symptoms: The sqlc code-generation pipeline fails after an em dash appears in a query or migration.
sections.diagnosis: Inspect the affected SQL or comments for that character in the pipeline described by the case.
sections.cause: The original case reports a pipeline failure on the character, without identifying a sqlc version or the underlying parser cause.
sections.remedy: Remove the em dash from SQL and comments in that affected pipeline.
sections.verification: The workaround is historical and context-specific; no current reproduction or supported universal rule is established.

cases.label: keep
cases.title: Empty string for an optional FK violates the constraint
cases.summary: Empty string for an optional FK violates the constraint

sections.context: An insert represents an absent optional foreign-key relationship.
sections.options: The case contrasts writing an empty string with a nil or skip-empty helper.
sections.decision: Represent the absent relationship with a nil or skip-empty helper in this schema.
sections.rationale: The original evidence states that the empty string is not a referenced key and violates the foreign-key constraint.
sections.consequences: Absence must follow the schema's nullable relationship semantics. The fixture does not identify a particular schema or test run.

cases.label: keep
cases.title: docker network removal breaks legacy composes that still attach to it
cases.summary: docker network removal breaks legacy composes that still attach to it

sections.symptoms: Other Compose stacks fail to start after a shared Docker network is removed.
sections.diagnosis: Find remaining Compose references to the network, especially external declarations, before removal.
sections.cause: The original case states that other stacks still declared the retired stack's network as external.
sections.remedy: Check remaining consumers before removing the shared network.
sections.verification: The fixture supplies no network name, current consumer inventory or completed retirement check.

cases.label: keep
cases.title: Webhook idempotency by a mutable status flag is replayable
cases.summary: Webhook idempotency by a mutable status flag is replayable

sections.symptoms: A replayed webhook repeats a grant when idempotency relies on a mutable status flag.
sections.diagnosis: Check whether the effect is gated by an atomic unique payment claim or by checking and setting mutable state.
sections.cause: The original case identifies the mutable flag as a replayable guard rather than an exactly-once claim.
sections.remedy: Gate the grant on the rows affected by a UNIQUE(payment_id) insert.
sections.verification: The original case has no incident timeline or impact measurement, so this is classified as a reusable troubleshooting pattern rather than a fabricated incident account.
